cards.explanation: The answer is that he curses the LORD's name. The text says the son of the Israelite woman "…blasphemed the Name with a curse." (Leviticus 24:11) A fight had broken out in the camp between him and an Israelite. After that, they brought him to Moses, Israel's leader.

The answer is that they place him in custody. The text says, "They placed him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them." (Leviticus 24:12) Nobody rushes a decision here, friends. They hold him and wait for the LORD to speak.

The answer is LORD. They hold him "…until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them." (Leviticus 24:12) So they wait. I know that's hard, friends, because waiting is a whole skill. Then the LORD speaks to Moses. (Leviticus 24:13)

The answer is all who heard him. The LORD says, "…have all who heard him lay their hands on his head; then have the whole assembly stone him." (Leviticus 24:14) The ones who heard it are the ones who lay on their hands. It's a heavy moment, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "the whole assembly must surely stone him, whether he is a foreign resident or native…" (Leviticus 24:16) The law covers both the foreign resident and the native. Same standard for everybody, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Whoever kills an animal must make restitution…" (Leviticus 24:18) So restitution is the answer for an animal. Then He says, "…whoever kills a man must be put to death." (Leviticus 24:21) Two different cases, friends, and two different outcomes.

The answer is the same injury he caused. The LORD says, "Just as he injured the other person, the same must be inflicted on him." (Leviticus 24:20) It's the same injury, no more and no less, friends. The law matches the harm.

The answer is that He is the LORD their God. The LORD says, "You are to have the same standard of law for the foreign resident and the native; for I am the LORD your God." (Leviticus 24:22) One LORD, one standard, friends. No special rules for who walks in the door, and no fine print. I wish my old junk drawer had run that fair.
